info.title: dssharness
info.description: Cross-platform repository harness CLI: git worktree management with Windows path-budget checks, driven entirely by .harness-config/config.json.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: DssHarness - cross-platform repository harness. Run 'dssharness help' for reference material.

commands.name: init
commands.description: Create .harness-config in the tree it runs in - a worktree's own included - with its configuration, its runner and connection-data directories, and the ignore rules that keep the untracked ones out of git.

options.name: --install-tools
options.description: Also install what each declared leg's host is missing, as install-missing-tools does. Off unless given. [default: False]

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Show detailed progress and child process output. [default: False]

options.name: --directory
options.description: Directory to operate in (default: current directory).

options.name: --no-prompt
options.description: Never ask for a superuser password; refuse a privileged install that needs one. [default: False]

commands.name: verify-git

commands.name: create-worktree
commands.description: Create a worktree under worktrees.root: .worktrees in a configuration init writes, .harness-config/worktrees where it names none.

options.name: --random
options.description: Generate the name instead of supplying one; the chosen name is reported. [default: False]

options.name: --verbose

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Worktree name: lowercase letters and digits joined by hyphens; at most 10 characters unless worktrees.maxNameLength says otherwise.

commands.name: delete-worktree
commands.description: Remove a worktree and everything under it, and its copies on hosts; refuses one holding work that would be lost, a locked one, or one whose evidence directories hold measurements, without --force.

options.name: --force
options.description: Delete the worktree without checking it, even when locked: uncommitted changes, commits on no branch, tag, remote-tracking ref, newest stash or other worktree's HEAD, and submodules' unpushed work are lost. [default: False]

options.name: --delete-evidence
options.description: Delete the configured evidence directories with the worktree. Every other check still runs. [default: False]

options.name: --discard-uncommitted
options.description: Delete the worktree's uncommitted changes with it, saying how many. Every other check still runs. [default: False]

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Show detailed progress and child process output. [default: False]

options.name: --directory
options.description: Directory to operate in (default: current directory).

options.name: --no-prompt

commands.name: create-agent
commands.description: Create an agent of an orchestrator: its record, its worktree, and its seed - the main tree's uncommitted state handed to it, each changed file copied and each deletion made, every path recorded; refused past the orchestrator's limit.

options.name: --model
options.description: The model the agent's session runs on, as its id.

options.name: --empty
options.description: Hand it nothing: record that it was made at a commit and given none of the main tree's uncommitted state. [default: False]

options.name: --session
options.description: The agent's Claude session id, or its subagent's id, whose transcripts delete-agent keeps. Run again, it records only this.

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Show detailed progress and child process output. [default: False]

options.name: --directory
options.description: Directory to operate in (default: current directory).

options.name: --no-prompt
options.description: Never ask for a superuser password; refuse a privileged install that needs one. [default: False]

arguments.name: ORCHESTRATOR
arguments.description: The orchestrator the agent works for.

arguments.name: AGENT
arguments.description: The agent's name, which names its directory and its worktree, orchestrator/agent under the worktrees root; never used twice.

commands.name: seed-agent
commands.description: Seed a live agent again with the main tree's uncommitted state; refused where its worktree holds changes of its own - a copy it was handed and left alone is not one - unless --force.

options.name: --empty
options.description: Hand it nothing more, and copy nothing: what it was handed before stays recorded. [default: False]

options.name: --force
options.description: Seed it though its worktree holds changes of its own, which the copies overwrite. [default: False]

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Show detailed progress and child process output. [default: False]

options.name: --directory
options.description: Directory to operate in (default: current directory).

options.name: --no-prompt
options.description: Never ask for a superuser password; refuse a privileged install that needs one. [default: False]

arguments.name: ORCHESTRATOR
arguments.description: The agent's orchestrator.

arguments.name: AGENT
arguments.description: The agent to seed again.

commands.name: refresh-agent
commands.description: Hand a live agent the main tree's changes under the paths, recorded as handed to it so its fold leaves them out; refused, copying nothing, where the agent changed or deleted one of them.

options.name: --apply
options.description: Hand them over; without it, only say what would be handed over. [default: False]

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Show detailed progress and child process output. [default: False]

options.name: --directory

arguments.description: The agent's orchestrator.

arguments.name: AGENT
arguments.description: The agent to refresh.

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: The paths to refresh, relative to the tree; the directory the anchor registries are kept in where none is given.

commands.name: fold-agent
commands.description: Fold a live agent's own changes into the main tree, then apply the anchor rows it filed: everything that refuses it is named before anything is written, the rows go in all or nothing, and a file of either tree that changed after it was weighed stops the fold part way (exit 21) rather than being written over or copied changed; its worktree is kept.

options.name: --apply
options.description: Write the fold and the rows; without it, only say what would be written. [default: False]

options.name: --settled
options.description: A path you reconciled in the main tree by hand, left out of the fold so the rest can go in: neither compared nor written. Once for each path.

options.name: --new
options.description: The id of a row the agent filed that the fold may make: a row no registry holds is otherwise refused, as a typo in an existing row's id would make it a second row. Once for each id.

options.name: --accept-lost
options.description: A cell of an existing row - trigger, closing, cross-refs - the fold may write though the agent's text does not keep its stored text word for word: read its word diff in the dry run first. Once for each cell.

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Show detailed progress and child process output. [default: False]

options.name: --directory
options.description: Directory to operate in (default: current directory).

options.name: --no-prompt
options.description: Never ask for a superuser password; refuse a privileged install that needs one. [default: False]

arguments.name: ORCHESTRATOR
arguments.description: The agent's orchestrator.

arguments.name: AGENT
arguments.description: The agent to fold.

commands.name: delete-agent
commands.description: Delete an agent: fold what is left of it and apply its rows, keep its evidence and transcripts, then remove its worktree and its copies on hosts; its directory stays as its history.

options.name: --apply
options.description: Do it; without it, only say what would be done. [default: False]

options.name: --settled
options.description: A path you reconciled in the main tree by hand, left out of the fold so the rest can go in: neither compared nor written. Once for each path.

options.name: --new
options.description: The id of a row the agent filed that the fold may make: a row no registry holds is otherwise refused, as a typo in an existing row's id would make it a second row. Once for each id.

options.name: --accept-lost
options.description: A cell of an existing row - trigger, closing, cross-refs - the fold may write though the agent's text does not keep its stored text word for word: read its word diff in the dry run first. Once for each cell.

options.name: --discard-uncommitted
options.description: Abandon the agent: fold nothing and apply no rows, and remove its worktree with its changes; its evidence and transcripts are still kept. [default: False]

commands.name: write-anchor
commands.description: Add a new anchor: to the pending registry, or to the done registry when its status is closed.

options.name: --priority
options.description: P0, the most urgent, to P5.

options.name: --priority-file
options.description: Read the priority from this file, as UTF-8; its trailing newline is not part of the cell. Cannot be combined with --priority.

options.name: --trigger
options.description: What is wrong, and what would make it worth doing now.

options.name: --trigger-file
options.description: Read the Trigger from this file, as UTF-8; its trailing newline is not part of the cell. Cannot be combined with --trigger.

options.name: --status
options.description: open, gated, disclosed or closed. A closed anchor is filed in the done registry. [default: open]

options.name: --status-file
options.description: Read the status from this file, as UTF-8; its trailing newline is not part of the cell. Cannot be combined with --status.

options.name: --closing
options.description: What remains to be done to close it.

options.name: --closing-file
options.description: Read the Closing work from this file, as UTF-8; its trailing newline is not part of the cell. Cannot be combined with --closing.

options.name: --cross-refs
options.description: Where it is cited, and related anchors.

options.name: --cross-refs-file
options.description: Read the Cross-refs from this file, as UTF-8; its trailing newline is not part of the cell. Cannot be combined with --cross-refs.

options.name: --anchor-dry-run
options.description: Show the anchor and where it would be filed, and write nothing. [default: False]

options.name: --verbose

options.name: --priority-file

options.name: --status

options.name: --status-file
options.description: Read the status from this file, as UTF-8; its trailing newline is not part of the cell. Cannot be combined with --status.

commands.name: check-anchor-citations
commands.description: Fail when an anchor id cited in a scanned root resolves to no row in either registry, or is cut where a line wraps at a hyphen. The roots come from anchors.citationRoots; nothing outside one is read. A break inside a segment, with no hyphen on either side, reads as the shorter id: keep every id whole on one line.

options.description: Check the files as HEAD holds them. This is the default. [default: False]

options.name: --branch

options.name: --limit

options.name: --run
options.description: Read these run ids, in the order given, instead of the newest runs.

options.name: --json
options.description: Write the per-leg result as JSON: success, errors, and whether a failure is a possible budget overrun. [default: False]

options.name: --verbose

options.name: --directory

options.name: --json

commands.name: sync
commands.description: Put each host's copy of this repository in step with this tree: files whose content changed are written, files the source no longer has are deleted, and the copy is verified afterwards. The tree is read once for every host; a file that changes before it is carried fails the sync.

options.name: --legs
options.description: Only the hosts these legs or leg sets run on: --legs a,b or --legs a b. Without it, every host a declared leg needs.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: List what would be written and deleted, and change nothing. [default: False]

options.name: --adopt
options.description: Take over these hosts' copies although the harness did not create them: --adopt vps or --adopt vps "wsl Ubuntu". Otherwise refused. What it would cost is reported either way.

options.name: --pull
options.description: Bring these paths back from each host's copy instead of syncing to it, verified on arrival.

options.name: --artifact
options.description: Carry one run's kept artifacts to each host instead of syncing the tree: --artifact 20260917-100000-0a1b2c3d. What a step kept is what a later step on another host reads.

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Show detailed progress and child process output. [default: False]

options.name: --directory
options.description: Directory to operate in (default: current directory).

options.name: --no-prompt
options.description: Never ask for a superuser password; refuse a privileged install that needs one. [default: False]

options.name: --use-staged

options.name: --no-prompt

commands.name: run
commands.description: Run a predefined runner across the legs it declares, with the same isolation, locking, stall bounds, witnesses and reporting build and test get.

options.name: --legs
options.description: Only these legs or leg sets: --legs a,b or --legs a b. Without it, the legs the runner declares.

options.name: --json
options.description: Write the per-leg ledger as JSON. [default: False]

options.name: --time
options.description: Pull runTimingRegex out of every step's output. [default: False]

options.name: --force-lock
options.description: Take a lock a run on another host holds. Always a human decision. [default: False]

options.name: --use-staged
options.description: Run against what is already staged on each host, without syncing again. Legs on a copy a sync or a takeover began and did not finish are inputs-moved. [default: False]

options.name: --input
options.description: Give one of the action's inputs a value for this run: --input name=value, once per input. Over the runner's .env values and the input's default; never a secret.

options.name: --manual-step
options.description: Run only these manual steps of the runner's action, each after the steps it needs: --manual-step a,b or --manual-step a --manual-step b. Without it, every step that is not manual, or the steps the runner names.

commands.name: host-exec
commands.description: Run a DssHarness command on a WSL distribution or an ssh host, in that host's copy of the tree it is typed in, installing or updating DssHarness there first when it is behind.

options.name: --ssh
options.description: Run on this ssh host, declared under hosts.ssh.

options.name: --wsl
options.description: Run in this WSL distribution, declared under hosts.wsl; with no name, WSL's default distribution.

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Show detailed progress and child process output. [default: False]

options.name: --directory
options.description: Directory to operate in (default: current directory).

options.name: --no-prompt
options.description: Never ask for a superuser password; refuse a privileged install that needs one. [default: False]

arguments.name: COMMAND
arguments.description: The DssHarness command to run there, with its arguments. Put -- before it, so its options stay its own.

commands.name: sync-serve
commands.description: Serve one sync operation on this host's copy of the repository. Not meant to be typed; the machine syncing runs it.

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Show detailed progress and child process output. [default: False]

options.name: --directory
options.description: Directory to operate in (default: current directory).

options.name: --no-prompt

arguments.name: OPERATION
arguments.description: The operation to perform on this host's copy.

arguments.name: ARGUMENTS
arguments.description: The operation's arguments: the copy's root, then whatever the operation takes.

commands.name: host-agent
commands.description: Serve one request from the DssHarness on another machine: a line of JSON on standard input, which stays open while it is served.

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Show detailed progress and child process output. [default: False]

commands.name: host-hold
commands.description: Hold this machine awake for the hold named, until a command's own keepAwake ends it or its time is up.
